speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. Can you describe the specific movements you are experiencing, such as tremors, stiffness, or involuntary jerking, and when did they first start?

speaker: Patient
text: 23-year-old college student. The patient is here for a follow-up appointment. He was recently diagnosed with schizophrenia and started on risperidone approximately 2 months ago. Reports a significant improvement in psychiatric symptoms since the start of treatment.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you experience any stiffness in your neck, shoulders, or trunk, and does it feel like your head is being pulled to one side or tilted backward? I also need to know if you have been taking any medication to counteract these symptoms or if you are currently on any other drugs.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Inability to remain still, persistent feeling of restlessness. I also have Frequent fidgeting, Repetitive crossing and uncrossing of legs, Pacing.

speaker: Doctor
text: The symptoms you describe, such as restlessness and the inability to remain still, are classic signs of akathisia, a common side effect of antipsychotic medications like risperidone. Do you feel an internal sense of anxiety or discomfort that drives this need to move, rather than just a physical tremor?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Recently diagnosed with schizophrenia. No other significant past medical history. Social history: College student, lives with parents. Denies tobacco, alcohol, or drug use.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the temporal relationship with starting risperidone and your description of inner restlessness, this is highly suggestive of drug-induced akathisia. To confirm this clinical diagnosis, I will reduce the risperidone dose or switch to an antipsychotic with a lower risk profile, and I may prescribe a beta-blocker like propranolol for symptomatic relief. DIAGNOSIS READY: Drug-induced akathisia
